action-bias.alt: Action bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. The urge to act can override evidence that waiting is the better choice.

additive-bias.alt: Additive bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. We often search for things to add before considering what to remove.

aestheticusability-effect.alt: Aesthetic–usability effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Attractive design can make a product feel more usable than it is.

agent-detection-bias.alt: Agent detection bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can infer an intentional agent before testing ordinary physical causes.

ambiguity-effect.alt: Ambiguity effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Unclear probabilities can make an option feel worse without evidence that it is.

anchoring-effect.alt: Anchoring effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. An irrelevant starting number can pull later estimates toward itself.

anthropocentric-thinking.alt: Anthropocentric thinking illustrated by Mira and Dex. Human experience can be a misleading starting point for understanding other organisms.

anthropomorphism.alt: Anthropomorphism illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can assign human feelings and intentions to things that do not have them.

apophenia.alt: Apophenia illustrated by Mira and Dex. Coincidences can feel like meaningful connections even without a real link.

assumed-similarity-bias.alt: Assumed similarity bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can assume other people share our preferences more than they actually do.

attentional-bias.alt: Attentional bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Current concerns can direct attention toward matching cues and away from other information.

attribute-substitution.alt: Attribute substitution illustrated by Mira and Dex. A difficult judgment can be replaced by an easier question without our noticing.

authority-bias.alt: Authority bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. A source's status can receive more weight than its relevant expertise warrants.

automation-bias.alt: Automation bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Automation can receive excessive trust even when direct evidence contradicts it.

availability-cascade.alt: Availability cascade illustrated by Mira and Dex. Public repetition and social uptake can make a belief seem increasingly credible.

availability-heuristic.alt: Availability heuristic illustrated by Mira and Dex. Events that come readily to mind can feel more frequent or likely.

backfire-effect.alt: Backfire effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Sometimes a correction strengthens a threatened belief. This response is not inevitable.

ballot-order-effect.alt: Ballot order effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Being listed first can give a candidate an advantage unrelated to merit.

bandwagon-effect.alt: Bandwagon effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Other people's choices can become the reason for our own.

barnum-effect.alt: Barnum effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Vague, broadly applicable descriptions can feel uniquely accurate about ourselves.

base-rate-neglect.alt: Base-rate neglect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Vivid individual details can crowd out information about how common each possibility is.

belief-bias.alt: Belief bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. A believable conclusion can make an invalid argument feel stronger.

ben-franklin-effect.alt: Ben Franklin effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Doing someone a favor can increase our liking for that person.

berksons-paradox.alt: Berkson's paradox illustrated by Mira and Dex. Conditioning on selection can create a misleading relationship between otherwise unrelated traits.

bias-blind-spot.alt: Bias blind spot illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can recognize bias in other people while overlooking it in ourselves.

bizarreness-effect.alt: Bizarreness effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Bizarre material can be easier to remember than ordinary material in some settings.

boundary-extension.alt: Boundary extension illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can remember a scene as including more surrounding space than we actually saw.

cheerleader-effect.alt: Cheerleader effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. A face can seem more attractive in a group than when viewed alone.

childhood-amnesia.alt: Childhood amnesia illustrated by Mira and Dex. Adults usually retain few autobiographical memories from their earliest childhood years.

choice-supportive-bias.alt: Choice-supportive bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. After choosing, we can remember the chosen option more favorably than the record supports.

clustering-illusion.alt: Clustering illusion illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can give small clusters in random data more meaning than they deserve.

cognitive-dissonance.alt: Cognitive dissonance illustrated by Mira and Dex. Conflicting beliefs and behavior can create discomfort that invites rationalization or change.

common-source-bias.alt: Common source bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Multiple reports can share one source, making apparent corroboration misleading.

compassion-fade.alt: Compassion fade illustrated by Mira and Dex. Compassion can weaken as victims become a larger, less identifiable group.

compromise-effect-choices-affected-if-pr.alt: Compromise effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. An option can become more attractive simply because it now occupies the middle.

confirmation-bias.alt: Confirmation bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can seek and retain supporting evidence more readily than evidence that challenges us.

congruence-bias.alt: Congruence bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Testing only confirming cases can leave competing explanations unexamined.

conjunction-fallacy.alt: Conjunction fallacy illustrated by Mira and Dex. A more detailed combination cannot be more probable than one of its own conditions.

conservatism-bias.alt: Conservatism bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can revise a belief too little when substantial new evidence arrives.

consistency-bias.alt: Consistency bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Present attitudes can make past attitudes seem more consistent than they were.

context-neglect-bias.alt: Context neglect bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. A technically neat solution can fail when people's actual circumstances are ignored.

continued-influence-effect.alt: Continued influence effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Corrected misinformation can continue influencing later reasoning.

contrast-effect.alt: Contrast effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. A recent contrasting stimulus can change how the next one appears.

courtesy-bias.alt: Courtesy bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. An expressed opinion can shift toward politeness to avoid offending someone.

cross-race-effect.alt: Cross-race effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Experience and familiarity can affect face recognition; people remain distinct individuals.

cryptomnesia.alt: Cryptomnesia illustrated by Mira and Dex. A remembered idea can feel original when its source has been forgotten.

cue-dependent-forgetting.alt: Cue-dependent forgetting illustrated by Mira and Dex. Recall can weaken without the cues associated with learning.

curse-of-knowledge.alt: Curse of knowledge illustrated by Mira and Dex. Knowing something well can make a beginner's difficulties harder to imagine.

declinism.alt: Declinism illustrated by Mira and Dex. A favorable view of the past can combine with an unjustifiably gloomy view of the future.

decoy-effect.alt: Decoy effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. An inferior third option can make a nearby target option more attractive.

default-effect.alt: Default effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. A preselected option can become a choice simply because it is already selected.

defensive-attribution-hypothesis.alt: Defensive attribution hypothesis illustrated by Mira and Dex. Perceived similarity to someone involved in a mishap can influence the blame assigned.

denomination-effect.alt: Denomination effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. The denomination of money can affect willingness to spend the same total.

disposition-effect.alt: Disposition effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can prefer selling gains while holding losses because of the purchase-price reference point.

distinction-bias.alt: Distinction bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Side-by-side comparison can exaggerate differences that matter little when options are experienced separately.

domain-neglect.alt: Domain neglect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Reasoning in an unfamiliar field can fail when relevant domain knowledge is ignored.

doubling-back-aversion.alt: Doubling-back aversion illustrated by Mira and Dex. Avoiding a return over old ground can keep us on a longer route.

dread-aversion.alt: Dread aversion illustrated by Mira and Dex. Anticipated dread can strongly influence when we choose to face an unpleasant event.

dunning-kruger-effect.alt: Dunning-Kruger effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Limited skill can make both performance and self-assessment harder to judge accurately.

duration-neglect.alt: Duration neglect illustrated by Mira and Dex. The length of an experience can receive surprisingly little weight in its overall evaluation.

effort-justification.alt: Effort justification illustrated by Mira and Dex. Effort invested in obtaining an outcome can inflate how highly we value it.

egocentric-bias.alt: Egocentric bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Our own perspective is easier to access and can receive disproportionate weight.

embodiment-bias.alt: Embodiment bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Our bodily capacities can shape what seems easy, reachable, or practical.

end-of-history-illusion.alt: End-of-history illusion illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can recognize substantial past change while underestimating how much we may change again.

endowment-effect.alt: Endowment effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Ownership alone can increase how much value we place on an object.

euphoric-recall.alt: Euphoric recall illustrated by Mira and Dex. Pleasant recollection can overshadow the negative parts of a past experience.

exaggerated-expectation.alt: Exaggerated expectation illustrated by Mira and Dex. Expectations can overshoot the size of the outcome that actually occurs.

experimenters-bias.alt: Experimenter's bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Researchers' expectations can influence which observations receive trust or attention.

extension-neglect.alt: Extension neglect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Quantity or sample size can receive too little weight in a judgment.

extrinsic-incentives-bias.alt: Extrinsic incentives bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can credit ourselves with inner motivation while assigning external motives to others.

fading-affect-bias.alt: Fading affect bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. The emotion attached to unpleasant memories can fade faster than emotion attached to pleasant ones.

false-consensus-effect.alt: False consensus effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can overestimate how many people share our views and preferences.

false-memory.alt: False memory illustrated by Mira and Dex. Imagination and reconstruction can sometimes be mistaken for memories of real events.

false-priors.alt: False priors illustrated by Mira and Dex. An incorrect prior belief can distort how new evidence is interpreted.

false-uniqueness-bias.alt: False uniqueness bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can overestimate how unusual our ideas, qualities, or projects are.

fluency-heuristic.alt: Fluency heuristic illustrated by Mira and Dex. Information that is easier to process can feel more credible or appealing.

form-function-attribution-bias.alt: Form function attribution bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. A robot's appearance can prompt mistaken expectations about its actual abilities.

framing-effect.alt: Framing effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Equivalent information can produce different judgments when described differently.

frequency-illusion.alt: Frequency illusion illustrated by Mira and Dex. Newly noticed things can feel newly common because we have started paying attention.

functional-fixedness.alt: Functional fixedness illustrated by Mira and Dex. An object's familiar purpose can hide other useful ways to use it.

fundamental-attribution-error.alt: Fundamental attribution error illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can overread other people's behavior as character and underread the situation.

g-i-joe-fallacy.alt: G. I. Joe fallacy illustrated by Mira and Dex. Knowing about a bias does not automatically prevent it from influencing us.

gamblers-fallacy.alt: Gambler's fallacy illustrated by Mira and Dex. Independent random events do not owe us a balancing outcome.

gender-bias.alt: Gender bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Gender assumptions can influence judgments beyond what a person's actual work shows.

gender-differences-in-eyewitness-memory.alt: Gender differences in eyewitness memory illustrated by Mira and Dex. Gender-related familiarity and attention can affect eyewitness detail under some conditions.

generation-effect.alt: Generation effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Information we generate ourselves can be easier to remember.

google-effect.alt: Google effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Expecting easy online access can reduce memory for the information itself.

group-attribution-error.alt: Group attribution error illustrated by Mira and Dex. One person's traits or one collective decision can be wrongly projected onto a whole group.

groupshift.alt: Groupshift illustrated by Mira and Dex. Group discussion can strengthen an initial lean toward risk or caution.

groupthink.alt: Groupthink illustrated by Mira and Dex. Protecting group harmony can suppress critical evaluation and dissent.

halo-effect.alt: Halo effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. One admired quality can spill into judgments about unrelated qualities.

hardeasy-effect.alt: Hard–easy effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can be overconfident on hard tasks and underconfident on easy ones.

hedonic-recall-bias.alt: Hedonic recall bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Current satisfaction can distort how pleasant or unpleasant the past seems.

hindsight-bias.alt: Hindsight bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Once an outcome is known, it can seem more predictable than it was beforehand.

hostile-attribution-bias.alt: Hostile attribution bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Ambiguous behavior can be interpreted as hostile before the evidence supports that reading.

hot-cold-empathy-gap.alt: Hot-cold empathy gap illustrated by Mira and Dex. A calm or comfortable state can make stronger future drives difficult to anticipate.

hot-hand-fallacy.alt: Hot-hand fallacy illustrated by Mira and Dex. A run of random successes can be mistaken for an increased chance of further success.

humor-effect.alt: Humor effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Humorous material can be more memorable than otherwise comparable information.

hyperbolic-discounting.alt: Hyperbolic discounting illustrated by Mira and Dex. Preferences can reverse when a smaller reward becomes immediately available.

illusion-of-asymmetric-insight.alt: Illusion of asymmetric insight illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can believe we understand others better than they understand us.

illusion-of-control.alt: Illusion of control illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can overestimate our influence over outcomes controlled largely by chance.

illusion-of-explanatory-depth.alt: Illusion of explanatory depth illustrated by Mira and Dex. A feeling of understanding can exceed our ability to explain the mechanism.

illusion-of-learning.alt: Illusion of learning illustrated by Mira and Dex. An explanation feeling clear does not guarantee that we can use it independently.

illusion-of-transparency.alt: Illusion of transparency illustrated by Mira and Dex. Our feelings and thoughts can seem more visible to others than they are.

illusion-of-validity.alt: Illusion of validity illustrated by Mira and Dex. A consistent-looking set of clues can produce more confidence than its predictive value deserves.

illusory-correlation.alt: Illusory correlation illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can perceive a relationship that the full pattern of evidence does not support.

illusory-superiority.alt: Illusory superiority illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can overestimate our desirable qualities relative to other people.

illusory-truth-effect.alt: Illusory truth effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Repeated statements can feel truer because they become easier to process.

impact-bias.alt: Impact bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can overestimate the intensity or duration of future feelings.

implicit-association.alt: Implicit association illustrated by Mira and Dex. Response speed can reflect how strongly ideas are associated in memory.

implicit-bias.alt: Implicit bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Unnoticed associations can influence how we interpret and treat other people.

impostor-syndrome.alt: Impostor Syndrome illustrated by Mira and Dex. People can doubt demonstrated competence and fear being exposed despite evidence of ability.

information-bias.alt: Information bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Seeking more information can feel useful even when it cannot affect the decision.

ingroup-bias.alt: Ingroup bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Membership in our own group can receive an advantage beyond the evidence.

insensitivity-to-sample-size.alt: Insensitivity to sample size illustrated by Mira and Dex. Small samples vary more, so a few observations deserve less confidence.

intentionality-bias.alt: Intentionality bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can attribute intention to actions that may have been accidental.

interoceptive-bias.alt: Interoceptive bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Hunger, fatigue, pain, and other bodily states can alter our judgments.

just-world-fallacy.alt: Just-world fallacy illustrated by Mira and Dex. A desire for a fair world can lead us to assign undeserved blame to people who suffer.

lag-effect.alt: Lag effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Spacing study sessions can support retention better than massing the same study time.

law-of-the-instrument.alt: Law of the instrument illustrated by Mira and Dex. A familiar tool or method can be applied where another approach fits better.

less-is-better-effect.alt: Less-is-better effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Separate evaluation can favor a smaller attractive set over a larger one.

leveling-and-sharpening.alt: Leveling and sharpening illustrated by Mira and Dex. Retelling can remove some details while emphasizing or exaggerating others.

levels-of-processing-effect.alt: Levels-of-processing effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Thinking about meaning can strengthen memory more than shallow processing.

list-length-effect.alt: List-length effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Longer lists can yield more recalled items but a smaller proportion recalled.

loss-aversion.alt: Loss aversion illustrated by Mira and Dex. A loss can feel worse than an equivalent gain feels good.

memory-inhibition.alt: Memory inhibition illustrated by Mira and Dex. Seeing part of a learned list can sometimes make its remaining items harder to recall.

mere-exposure-effect.alt: Mere exposure effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Repeated exposure can increase liking or comfort even without new reasons.

misinformation-effect.alt: Misinformation effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Information received after an event can alter memory of the event itself.

misinterpreted-effort-hypothesis.alt: Misinterpreted-effort hypothesis illustrated by Mira and Dex. Learning that feels effortful can be mistaken for learning that is ineffective.

modality-effect.alt: Modality effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. The final items of a list can be recalled better when heard than when read.

money-illusion.alt: Money illusion illustrated by Mira and Dex. A larger money amount can hide a decline in purchasing power.

mood-congruent-memory-bias.alt: Mood-congruent memory bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Current mood can make emotionally matching memories easier to retrieve.

moral-credential.alt: Moral credential illustrated by Mira and Dex. A prior good deed can become an excuse for later behavior we would otherwise reject.

moral-luck.alt: Moral luck illustrated by Mira and Dex. Luck in an outcome can affect moral judgments about otherwise similar conduct.

motivated-reasoning.alt: Motivated reasoning illustrated by Mira and Dex. A desired conclusion can bend how evidence is evaluated and explained.

motonormativity.alt: Motonormativity illustrated by Mira and Dex. Normalizing car use can make its harms less noticeable than comparable harms from other sources.

naive-cynicism.alt: Naïve cynicism illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can expect more self-serving distortion in others than in ourselves.

naive-realism.alt: Naïve realism illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can treat our own perspective as plain reality and disagreement as others' error.

negativity-bias.alt: Negativity bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Negative information can receive more psychological weight than comparable positive information.

neglect-of-probability.alt: Neglect of probability illustrated by Mira and Dex. Vivid possible consequences can crowd out the probability that they will occur.

next-in-line-effect.alt: Next-in-line effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Preparing our own turn can impair memory for the person who speaks just before us.

non-adaptive-choice-switching.alt: Non-adaptive choice switching illustrated by Mira and Dex. A bad outcome can prompt abandoning the better option even when conditions have not changed.

normalcy-bias.alt: Normalcy bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Expecting familiar normality can delay recognition of a changed situation.

not-invented-here.alt: Not invented here illustrated by Mira and Dex. An outside origin can become a reason to reject a useful idea.

objectivity-illusion.alt: Objectivity illusion illustrated by Mira and Dex. Feeling objective does not guarantee that our judgments are free from bias.

observer-expectancy-effect.alt: Observer-expectancy effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. An observer's expectations can unintentionally shape procedures and measurements.

omission-bias.alt: Omission bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Harm caused by inaction can seem more acceptable than comparable harm caused by action.

optimism-bias.alt: Optimism bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can overestimate favorable outcomes and underestimate difficulties for our own plans.

ostrich-effect.alt: Ostrich effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Avoiding unwelcome information can feel better briefly while leaving the underlying problem unaddressed.

outcome-bias.alt: Outcome bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. A lucky result can make a poor decision process look better than it was.

outgroup-favoritism.alt: Outgroup favoritism illustrated by Mira and Dex. Outside-group status can sometimes receive an advantage over one's own group.

outgroup-homogeneity-bias.alt: Outgroup homogeneity bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can see less variation within other groups than within our own.

overconfidence-effect.alt: Overconfidence effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Confidence can exceed what the evidence justifies.

pareidolia.alt: Pareidolia illustrated by Mira and Dex. Ambiguous visual patterns can look like familiar faces or objects.

part-list-cueing-effect.alt: Part-list cueing effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Partial-list cues can sometimes interfere with recall of the remaining items.

peakend-rule.alt: Peak–end rule illustrated by Mira and Dex. The peak and the ending can strongly influence our memory of an experience.

perky-effect.alt: Perky effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. A faint perceived image can influence imagery while being mistaken for imagination.

persistence.alt: Persistence illustrated by Mira and Dex. Distressing memories can recur involuntarily after the event has ended.

pessimism-bias.alt: Pessimism bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can overestimate the likelihood of unfavorable outcomes.

phantom-effect.alt: Phantom effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. An unavailable option can continue influencing choices among the options we actually have.

picture-superiority-effect.alt: Picture superiority effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Pictures can be easier to remember than equivalent information presented only as words.

placement-bias.alt: Placement bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Self-placement against others can follow our own strengths and weaknesses without adequate comparison.

plan-continuation-bias.alt: Plan continuation bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. A once-reasonable plan can persist after circumstances make it unsuitable.

planning-fallacy.alt: Planning fallacy illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can underestimate task duration by overlooking delays and necessary steps.

plant-blindness.alt: Plant blindness illustrated by Mira and Dex. Plants can fade into the background of our attention despite their importance.

positivity-effect.alt: Positivity effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Older adults can show a relative preference for positive information in memory.

present-bias.alt: Present bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Immediate costs and rewards can outweigh larger later consequences.

prevention-bias.alt: Prevention bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Prevention can be favored beyond what its effectiveness relative to detection or response warrants.

primacy-effect.alt: Primacy effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Items near the beginning of a sequence can have a memory advantage.

pro-innovation-bias.alt: Pro-innovation bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Excitement about an innovation can overshadow its limitations and possible drawbacks.

probability-matching.alt: Probability matching illustrated by Mira and Dex. Matching choice frequencies to outcome frequencies can perform worse than always choosing the likelier outcome.

processing-difficulty-effect.alt: Processing difficulty effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Some forms of effortful processing can strengthen later memory.

projection-bias.alt: Projection bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can assume our future preferences will resemble our current state too closely.

proportionality-bias.alt: Proportionality bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can expect a large event to require a correspondingly large or elaborate cause.

pseudocertainty-effect.alt: Pseudocertainty effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. An outcome can feel certain when we mentally set aside an earlier unresolved risk.

puritanical-bias.alt: Puritanical bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. A moral-failure explanation can crowd out the social conditions shaping behavior.

pygmalion-effect.alt: Pygmalion effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Others' expectations can affect performance through the opportunities and treatment they provide.

quantification-bias.alt: Quantification bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Measurable quantities can receive more weight than important values that are harder to quantify.

reactance.alt: Reactance illustrated by Mira and Dex. A perceived threat to freedom can increase attraction to the restricted choice.

reactive-devaluation.alt: Reactive devaluation illustrated by Mira and Dex. A proposal can seem worse simply because it came from an adversary.

recency-effect.alt: Recency effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Items at the end of a sequence can be especially easy to recall immediately.

recency-illusion.alt: Recency illusion illustrated by Mira and Dex. Recently noticing a phenomenon can make it seem recently created.

conservatism-or-regressive-bias.alt: Regressive bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Recalled extreme values can drift toward more moderate values.

reminiscence-bump.alt: Reminiscence bump illustrated by Mira and Dex. People often recall many autobiographical events from adolescence and early adulthood.

repetition-blindness.alt: Repetition blindness illustrated by Mira and Dex. Rapidly repeated items can be missed as separate occurrences.

restraint-bias.alt: Restraint bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can overestimate our ability to resist temptation when it is present.

rhyme-as-reason-effect.alt: Rhyme as reason effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Rhyming statements can feel more convincing without stronger evidence.

risk-compensation.alt: Risk compensation illustrated by Mira and Dex. Feeling protected can encourage behavior that gives back some of the safety benefit.

rosy-retrospection.alt: Rosy retrospection illustrated by Mira and Dex. Past experiences can be remembered as more pleasant than they felt at the time.

salience-bias.alt: Salience bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Striking information can capture attention at the expense of less vivid but relevant details.

saying-is-believing-effect.alt: Saying is believing effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Adapting a message to an audience can shift what we later remember as our own view.

scope-neglect.alt: Scope neglect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Our response can change too little when the scale of a problem changes greatly.

selection-bias.alt: Selection bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. A sample selected in a skewed way may not represent the population of interest.

selective-perception.alt: Selective perception illustrated by Mira and Dex. Expectations can influence what we notice and how we interpret it.

self-relevance-effect.alt: Self-relevance effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Information linked to ourselves can receive a memory advantage.

self-serving-bias.alt: Self-serving bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can claim credit for success while shifting responsibility for failure outward.

semmelweis-reflex.alt: Semmelweis reflex illustrated by Mira and Dex. Evidence can be rejected too quickly because it conflicts with an established framework.

serial-position-effect.alt: Serial position effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Items at the beginning and end of a sequence often outlast those in the middle.

sexual-overperception-bias.alt: Sexual overperception bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Ambiguous friendliness can be mistaken for sexual interest; assumptions are not confirmation.

shared-information-bias.alt: Shared information bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Groups can overdiscuss shared facts while neglecting information held by only one member.

social-comparison-bias.alt: Social comparison bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can favor candidates who feel less threatening to our own strengths.

social-cryptomnesia.alt: Social cryptomnesia illustrated by Mira and Dex. A society can remember a change while forgetting the people who helped bring it about.

social-desirability-bias.alt: Social desirability bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can report more approved behavior and less embarrassing behavior than the record supports.

source-confusion.alt: Source confusion illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can remember information while confusing where or how we learned it.

spacing-effect.alt: Spacing effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Learning spread across time can support longer retention than one concentrated exposure.

spotlight-effect.alt: Spotlight effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can overestimate how much other people notice our appearance or mistakes.

status-quo-bias.alt: Status quo bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. The existing arrangement can receive preference merely because it is already in place.

stereotype-bias-or-stereotypical-bias.alt: Stereotype memory bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Memory can drift toward familiar stereotypes rather than the details actually observed.

stereotyping.alt: Stereotyping illustrated by Mira and Dex. A group label can substitute for evidence about an individual.

subadditivity-effect.alt: Subadditivity effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Separate estimates for exclusive possibilities can add up to more than the estimate for their whole.

subjective-validation.alt: Subjective validation illustrated by Mira and Dex. A claim can feel valid because it fits our beliefs or experience, without adequate independent evidence.

suffix-effect.alt: Suffix effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. An irrelevant sound after a spoken list can reduce the memory advantage of its final items.

suggestibility.alt: Suggestibility illustrated by Mira and Dex. Suggested details can become incorporated into later recollection.

sunk-cost-effect.alt: Sunk cost effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Past investment can keep us committed after the forward-looking case has weakened.

surrogation.alt: Surrogation illustrated by Mira and Dex. A measure of a goal can quietly become a substitute for the goal itself.

survivorship-bias.alt: Survivorship bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Visible successes can mislead when the failures that dropped out are missing.

system-justification.alt: System justification illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can defend an existing social arrangement because it feels established and legitimate.

systematic-bias.alt: Systematic bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Unequal regression toward a baseline can systematically distort comparisons.

tachypsychia.alt: Tachypsychia illustrated by Mira and Dex. Intense stress or arousal can change how quickly time seems to pass.

teleological-bias.alt: Teleological bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. A useful role can be mistaken for the purpose that explains a natural thing's existence.

telescoping-effect.alt: Telescoping effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Events can be remembered as more recent or more distant than they actually were.

testing-effect.alt: Testing effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Practicing retrieval can strengthen later memory more than rereading alone.

third-person-effect.alt: Third-person effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can expect media messages to influence others more than ourselves.

time-saving-bias.alt: Time-saving bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Equal speed increases do not produce equal time savings; the starting speed matters.

tip-of-the-tongue.alt: Tip of the tongue illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can partly retrieve a memory while the exact word remains inaccessible.

trait-ascription-bias.alt: Trait ascription bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can see our own behavior as variable while treating other people's traits as more fixed.

travis-syndrome.alt: Travis syndrome illustrated by Mira and Dex. The present moment can feel more unique, important, or permanent than the evidence warrants.

truth-bias.alt: Truth bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. We often begin by accepting communicated information before checking its accuracy.

turkey-illusion.alt: Turkey illusion illustrated by Mira and Dex. A long stable pattern does not guarantee that a sudden break cannot occur.

ultimate-attribution-error.alt: Ultimate attribution error illustrated by Mira and Dex. We can explain our group's mistakes situationally while treating another group's mistakes as character.

unit-bias.alt: Unit bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. A standard package or serving can seem like the right amount simply because it is one unit.

value-selection-bias.alt: Value selection bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Available numbers can attract answers even when the task requires deriving a different value.

verbatim-effect.alt: Verbatim effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. We often retain the general meaning better than the exact wording.

von-restorff-effect.alt: Von Restorff effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. An item that differs from its surroundings can receive a memory advantage.

weberfechner-law.alt: Weber–Fechner law illustrated by Mira and Dex. A fixed change is often less noticeable against a larger starting quantity.

well-travelled-road-effect.alt: Well travelled road effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Familiar routes can feel shorter in duration than unfamiliar ones.

women-are-wonderful-effect.alt: Women are wonderful effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Positive gender stereotypes can still replace evidence about individual people.

worse-than-average-effect.alt: Worse-than-average effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Difficulty can make us underestimate our performance relative to others facing the same challenge.

zeigarnik-effect.alt: Zeigarnik effect illustrated by Mira and Dex. Interrupted or unfinished tasks can remain especially accessible in memory.

zero-risk-bias.alt: Zero-risk bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. Eliminating a small risk can feel better than making a larger reduction in another risk.

zero-sum-bias.alt: Zero-sum bias illustrated by Mira and Dex. One person's gain does not always require another person's loss.
